title: Quarterly roadmap interlock: mini-simulations & executive decision rubric
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Produce a compact, simulation-driven briefing packet for senior leadership and the board that surfaces 3 disciplined roadmap scenarios (Accelerate, Rebalance, Protect Runway) with clear decision rubrics and rollback lanes.

Scope and deliverables:
- Short PRD (1 page) summarizing candidate initiatives and quantitative levers (cost, latency, reliability, time-to-market).
- Three run-theatre mini-simulations (5-7 minute scenarios each) that walk execs through inputs, expected outcomes, and failure modes.
- Decision rubric with measurable thresholds: customer impact, SLO risk delta, incremental monthly run cost, and engineering runway (FTE weeks).
- A one-page rollback and fallback playbook per scenario (canary gating, automatic fallback model variants, cross-region failover).
- Readout deck (10 slides) and a 20-minute dry run script for execs.

Context and rationale:
Executive feedback from last QBR emphasized the need for succinct, trade-off oriented choices rather than long lists of initiatives. This ticket codifies an approach that replaces a long catalog with scenario-driven asks and concrete rollback lanes so leadership can make quick, confident decisions. The interlock element means product, eng, infra, and finance run aligned simulations and surface a single recommended lane with 1 alternate and 1 deferred lane.

Key assumptions:
- Cost estimates use unit economics from runtime-1.18 benchmarks and current Dedicated capacity pricing.
- Reliability impacts are evaluated against current SLO baselines in the Console observability dashboards.
- Engineering runway estimated from current sprint capacity plus projected hiring cadence.

Major trade-offs identified:
- Invest in batching/kernel optimization (high one-time engineering cost, large downstream op-economics) vs. prioritize Console UX improvements (lower engineering cost, faster customer-facing wins).
- Prioritize Dedicated capacity expansion for large customers (revenue certainty) vs. invest in Private deployment compliance (longer sales cycles, strategic enterprise wins).

Artifacts and links:
- PRD draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/roadmap/quarterly-mini-prd-240681 (working doc)
- Readout deck draft: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1QBR_240681_deck
- Simulation runbook (spreadsheet): https://sheets.redwood.ai/d/mini-sims-240681
- Cost model (runtime economics): https://dashboards.redwood.ai/costs/runtime-2026-Q2
- Related GitHub issues: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-platform/pulls?q=is%3Apr+240681

Success criteria:
- Deck and decision rubric approved by PM and VP Eng by 2026-03-18.
- Smooth dry run with Exec (no more than 3 clarification questions flagged as blockers).
- Board-ready packet completed and uploaded to secure folder by 2026-03-20.

Next steps:
1) Finalize PRD and assign engineering leads to produce the cost/reliability delta numbers (owner: Liam).
2) Run cross-functional simulation workshop on 2026-03-08 (owner: Aisha).
3) Update deck with scenario outputs and run dry run on 2026-03-17 (owner: Liam + Marta Reyes).
4) Lock the recommended lane and produce rollback playbooks by 2026-03-19.

Notes on stakeholder expectations:
- Finance wants transparent assumptions for incremental MRR and unit cost savings; include a short appendix with formulas.
- Legal flagged a potential compliance gating for Private deployments; include a legal comment in each scenario.
- Sales requested one slide with customer-commitment impact per lane.

Operational risks:
- If engineering estimates slip >20%, the Accelerate lane is not achievable within Q2 and should be deprioritized.
- If Console SLO degradation risk exceeds 5% variance on key customers, require canary expansion before rollout.

Owner notes: Please add meeting notes and tag the ticket when you update the PRD or deck. Use the labels to control visibility during board prep (sensitive + exec).
